notes:
Scenario: utm_data jsonb persistence across variations on the password #create path (POST http://app.lvh.me:5007/api/v1/sign_up, application/json). Workflow: qa_harness cleanup then seed default-user-and-org.json (both succeeded, 29 seed steps). Ran four real HTTP signups (fresh emails, valid password) then verified each created User's persisted utm_data via test_frr /tmp/sr6_verify.rb (login-shell + cd form). All four POSTs returned HTTP 200 and created users (ids 39324-39327).

CASE A (multi-key {utm_medium:'cpc', utm_term:'kw', utm_content:'ad1', utm_id:'x'}): persisted utm_data.inspect = {"utm_id"=>"x", "utm_term"=>"kw", "utm_medium"=>"cpc", "utm_content"=>"ad1"}; class Hash; key classes [String]; value classes [String]; == expected(string-keyed Hash) => true. Raw jsonb before type cast = "{\"utm_id\": \"x\", \"utm_term\": \"kw\", \"utm_medium\": \"cpc\", \"utm_content\": \"ad1\"}" (proper JSON object in Postgres). Note: Postgres jsonb does not preserve key insertion order, but Ruby Hash == is order-independent so equality holds and no data is lost.

CASE B (single-key {utm_medium:'email'}): persisted utm_data.inspect = {"utm_medium"=>"email"}; class Hash; == {'utm_medium'=>'email'} => true; string keys/values.

CASE C (special/numeric-looking {utm_term:'a b&c=d', utm_content:'123'}): persisted utm_data.inspect = {"utm_term"=>"a b&c=d", "utm_content"=>"123"}; class Hash; == expected => true; round-trip intact incl. space, '&', '=' in the value and '123' kept as the STRING "123" (not coerced to Integer); key classes [String], value classes [String].

CASE D adversarial (utm_data:"notahash" JSON scalar string): NO crash, HTTP 200, User created (id 39327); persisted utm_data.inspect = nil; class NilClass; utm_data.nil? => true. The sign_up_params permit (utm_data: {}) drops the non-hash scalar to nil exactly as expected; column is nil, never {}.

Across all cases utm_source/utm_campaign/internal_ref were nil (not sent), confirming absent params => nil. No jsonb corruption, no key-type change, no value coercion, no data loss on the normal multi-key object. Empty findings array reflects genuine runtime scrutiny: the password #create path persists utm_data jsonb correctly for multi-key, single-key, special-char/numeric-string, and adversarial-scalar inputs.
